correctness.rationale: For each nonroot vertex \(j\), its survival as a rooted leaf has probability \((j-1)/(n-1)\). For distinct labels the covariance of its leaf indicator with each subsequent attachment to \(i\) telescopes to the stated off-diagonal covariance; on the diagonal \(D_jY_j=0\) gives the negative covariance. Exact row summation yields the nonroot birth-age formula. Its second discrete difference equals \(1/[i(n-1)]>0\) for the stated range, establishing ordered sign blocks, with an empty positive block allowed for small sizes. A harmonic-sum limit gives \(f(x)=(1-x)/2+x\log x\) and its unique interior zero near \(0.284668\). Exact-rational enumeration of 46,233 parent arrays through nine vertices and 34,860 assertions supplements, but does not replace, the universal proof.

value.rationale: The birth-labeled degree–leaf covariance is a natural stochastic dependence statistic in a canonical growing random tree. Completing all nonroot cross-covariance rows yields a nontrivial strict convexity mechanism and a sharp asymptotic positive-to-negative covariance threshold at about 28.5 percent of vertex birth time. The already published root-only positivity cannot predict a sign reversal for later vertices. The exact finite and limiting statements offer a structural diagnostic for age-dependent effects, while not asserting an external downstream theorem.
